- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.  
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to stay above; if below, stays below — adjust for 1–2 day lag.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price if sentiment is rising; overestimates if sentiment is falling — adjust forecast in direction of sentiment trend.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.8, -0.4, +0.6), model fails to capture momentum shifts; apply smoothing or trend-following correction.
